name: Bounded Fleet — compliance-boundary cards, skill-level specialists, one door, one release id
thesis: An Agent Card is a compliance unit — its own persona, authority envelope, data_class, regulator surface, eval/redteam suite and canary (schema.py CardIdentity/CardEval/CardExperiment; compile.py G7/G8/G12) — so the fleet should have exactly as many cards as there are compliance boundaries (today four: Intake, Collections, Insurance, Supervisor; a Hardship or Lapse boundary is plausible, a "PTP specialist" is not). Every finer specialisation is a Skill Pack, which already carries its own allowed-tools, eval_suite, data_class and mouth in frontmatter (packs/ptp-negotiate/SKILL.md:114-134) and already swaps in and out as one developer message without touching the cached system prefix (skills/runtime.py:SKILL_BODY_PREFIX, load_skill; voice/tools.py:2810-2825). What is missing is not more cards but the three mechanisms that make the four cards a fleet instead of a monolith with decoration: a Door that picks the card before the prompt is built (today routing.py:34-45 returns env BOT_ID and bot.py:427 loads the bundle before it knows who is calling), a Handoff that really swaps prompt, grant, flow and context under a typed Carry (today tools.py:2773-2808 and bot_tools.py:432-449 write handler_bot_id and change nothing the model sees), and a Fleet Release that pins every card, flow, skill and door version live at one instant under one id so a multi-agent call still has one version number. Skill activation becomes authored data (replacing runtime.py:INTENT_TO_SKILL), skills get their own graph, evals and entry conditions in the studio, and evals are cached by content hash so a new specialist costs its own fixtures plus nothing. Agents communicate through typed Carries, flow variables and a fleet event bus — structured, logged, off the model's word — and the design says plainly where it cannot go: a boundary hop is a new system prefix and therefore one prompt-cache miss, which is amortised (warm per-deployment prefixes, prefetch at edge eligibility, a bridging entry line) but not abolished, and no agent negotiates with another agent in free text on the audio path.
primitives: Agent Card (compliance boundary) — owns identity, persona/voice refs, tool include∪locked, handoffs, skills, policy bindings, human gates, outbound, eval, experiment. Is: agent_core/cards/schema.py AgentCard, stored on prompt_versions.agent_card (sql/09_bot_config.sql:125), one published row per bot (ux_prompt_versions_one_published_per_bot), one active bot_deployments row per bot+env. Gains: identity.boundary {authority_profile, persona_distinct: bool} used by new gate G16; handoffs[].carry_schema (the existing, empty CardHandoff.payload_schema made typed and enforced), handoffs[].entry_node, handoffs[].announce_line, handoffs[].voice: keep|switch; door: {accepts_intents[], accepts_objectives[], is_default_for_channels[]}; memory.max_hops_per_call (default 2). One card = one deployment_id = one system-prefix cache key.

Skill Pack (specialist) — owns procedure, allowed-tools, eval fixtures, entry conditions, exit carry. Is: agent_core/skills/pack.py SkillPack + packs/*/SKILL.md, persisted/signed in skills, skill_versions, skill_attachments (sql/15_skills.sql). Gains frontmatter: activation {intents[] ⊂ understanding allowed set, objectives[] ⊂ flow_graph.OBJECTIVES, flow_nodes[] (node keys of the host card), variables{key: value} over flows_dynamic.SESSION_VARIABLES ∪ extractVariables}; entry_line; exit.carry[] (variable keys it promises to fill); eval_suite (exists: 'skill.ptp-negotiate') becomes a real eval_suites row. Activation replaces the hardcoded INTENT_TO_SKILL dict (skills/runtime.py:27-35) and the gated_upsell pre-action; grant is unchanged — pack attachment at publish is still the permission boundary (ADR-0001).

Door (inbound router) — owns 'which card answers this contact' and nothing else. New: agent_core/cards/door.py + table door_rules(id, tenant_id, version, priority, channel, to_number_or_pool, conditions jsonb over caller features {known_customer, dpd, open_ptp, product_interest, callback_pending, lead_open, language_pref}, first_utterance_intent nullable, target_bot_id) + door_decisions(interaction_id|conversation_id, door_version, rule_id, target_deployment_id, decided_at). Tier 0 is deterministic (features come from voice/twilio_ops.lookup_customer_for_caller, already called at bot.py:504, moved ahead of load_active_bundle at bot.py:427). Tier 1 is the Door Card: intake-v1 (defaults.py:158-174, already carrying verify-and-disclose and a handoff allowlist) runs greet_disclose → discover_intent → verify_identity, then a flow expression edge — not the model — calls the Handoff with the door's intent→card mapping. Replaces routing.py:runtime_entry_bot_id() env BOT_ID (.env.example:108), db.DEFAULT_BOT_ID in deployment.py:load_active_bundle, and the literal 'kaia-v2-4' at db.py:7114.

Mission (outbound door) — exists: mission.py (Action Contract + card + book), call_attempts(bot_id, deployment_id, objective, decision_id, policy_version) (sql/21_outbound.sql:20-75). Gains: card resolution from card.outbound.objectives — the card that declares the objective dials it (new gate G-OB10: exactly one production card per objective per number_pool, else an explicit priority on the Door screen). The voice worker loads the bundle by the attempt's pinned deployment_id (bot.py:487-499 already reads attempt_id/objective/treatment_decision_id from Twilio params) rather than 'whatever is active now', falling back to active and recording the fallback.

Carry (typed handoff payload) — owns what one agent tells the next. New: agent_core/cards/carry.py Carry pydantic model: identity {verified: bool, method ∈ catalog.VERIFY_METHODS, turn_index}, call_goal, call_goal_intent, intent, sentiment, language, objective, decision_id, mission constraints {allowed_offers, max_duration_sec, upsell_blocked reason}, flow_variables (voice/flow_vars.FlowVariables bag), summary (agent_core/compaction.extractive_summary — deterministic, 0 ms), open_commitments (voice/memory.py SQL half, never the LLM half), reco_shortlist_ids, announce_line. Constructed only by the runtime (voice/handoff.py, bot_tools.py), never from model arguments — the model's handoff tool keeps only target_bot_id and reason. Validated against the caller's handoffs[].carry_schema and the target's handoff entry-node requirements (G18). Persisted to new handoff_events(id, interaction_id, from_deployment_id, to_deployment_id, turn_index, carry jsonb, prefix_cache_hit bool, hop_ms, fleet_release_id).

Bundle Swap (handoff executor) — owns the mechanical hop on voice. New: voice/handoff.py swap(session, target_bot_id, carry) = load_active_bundle(bot_id=target, customer_id) (deployment.py, canary-aware via canary.pick_deployment_id) → resolve_mouth + ToolGrant.for_bundle (skills/runtime.py, tools/grant.py) → build_tools registry rebuilt (voice/tools.py:2916-2919 filter) → build_authored_flow(target graph, entry_node = handoffs[].entry_node or the target node with entryFor ['handoff']) → flow_manager.set_node_from_config (already how flows_dynamic runs 'always' edges) with the target's role message → optional TTSUpdateSettingsFrame voice switch → session.deployment_id, interactions.handler_bot_id (db_inbox.py:1441) → handoff_events row → fleet event publish. Replaces voice/mesh.py activate_role/MeshState, the mesh_activate_insurance action (bot.py:1518), _on_upsell_engaged mesh call (bot.py:1043-1067), BOT_TO_MESH_ROLE (defaults.py:46-51) and handoff_policy.py.

Prefix Warmer — owns the amortisation of hop cost. New: voice/prefix_warm.py: on publish and every ~4 minutes, for every active production deployment on this voice worker, send the exact system prefix (bot._system_instruction_from_bundle + skill description block) with max_tokens=1 on the voice LLM so the provider-side prompt cache (Azure: ≥1024-token prefix, evicted after 5–10 min idle per current docs; vLLM on-prem: process-local automatic prefix caching) stays hot per card. Extends the existing boot warm in bot.py:2455-2510 (_warm_llm_service) from one bundle to the active fleet. Plus prefetch: when a flow enters a node whose functions include handoff_to_agent, or reco returns a non-empty shortlist, the target bundle is loaded and its grant/flow compiled in the background so the hop pays only the LLM's first token.

Tool Grant / Offer — unchanged owner: agent_core/tools/grant.py (ADR-0001/0002): card ∪ packs ∪ connectors ∪ VOICE_ALWAYS; offer ⊆ grant. The swap builds a new grant from the target card; carry cannot add a tool; skill activation changes the offer only.

Flow — owns the conversation graph per card. Is: flow_graph.py (schema, entryFor, RESERVED_NODE_KEYS) executed by voice/flows_dynamic.py. Gains: entryFor value 'handoff' (a node a received handoff lands on; G18 requires it on any card that is a handoff target); a generic 'handoff' flow action {target} replacing mesh_activate_insurance; node-entry skill activation post-action; and a text projection flow_text.py that runs the same graph on WhatsApp (current node key kept in conversations.bot_state; node tools = offer; go_to_* transitions as tools; expression/always edges evaluated deterministically after each tool result) so the flow is no longer voice-only (bot_runtime.py today is prompt+tools).

Closer + Post-call — exist: call_closer.py (call_outcomes two-axis), post_call_actions.py (authored on_outcome verbs), cadence.py, voice/memory.py. Gains: call_outcomes.hops jsonb (deployment ids with turn ranges, from handoff_events); rule of ownership: on_outcome rules from the card that produced the outcome (last handler), cadence and stop_on from the mission's card; the Supervisor brief card consumes the Carry when escalate_to_human is warm — an internal agent reading another agent's typed output.

Fleet Release (the one version number) — new: fleet_releases(id, tenant_id, created_at, created_by, manifest jsonb {door_version, cards: {bot_id: {deployment_id, prompt_version_id, card_hash, flow_hash, skill_version_ids[]}}, policy_version, grader_version}, manifest_hash, prev_hash) appended inside every publish transaction next to agent_core/change_log.py (same hash-chain pattern), plus fleet_release_id columns on interactions, call_attempts, conversations/messages (per turn on text), handoff_events, door_decisions. Derived, never authored: a publish of any card or door version yields a new release.

Compiler — is: agent_core/cards/compile.py G0–G15, G-OB1–9. Adds: G16 boundary_distinct (two production cards with identical persona hash, authority_profile, data_class, regulator_tags → fail with 'this is a skill, not a card'); G17 door_coverage (every channel/pool has a resolvable default; no dead door rule; door targets are deployed); G18 carry_compat (every handoff edge: target has a handoff entry node, carry_schema ⊇ target entry-node requirements, identity carried only if target's entry node skips verify, hop cycles ≤ memory.max_hops_per_call, promotional target requires promo-consent check); G19 skill_activation (activation intents in the understanding vocabulary, nodes exist on the host graph, no two attached skills claim the same (intent, node) without priority); G20 eval_cache (regression/redteam may pass via a cached report when (card_hash, skill_version set, flow_hash, grader_version) is unchanged — reported as 'pass · cached r-…', never as skipped); G21 prefix_budget (target card's static prefix token count ≤ configured hop budget so a cold miss is bounded); G-OB10 objective_owner.

Eval Suites — exist: eval_suites/eval_tasks/eval_redteam_cases/eval_reports/eval_trials (sql/14_agent_factory.sql), code graders (eval/graders.py), fixtures, canary (canary.py). Becomes three tiers keyed by content hash: skill suite (skill.<slug>), card suite (boundary tasks + union of attached skill suites), fleet suite (door fixtures and carry fixtures).

Fleet Events — is: voice/mesh_bus.py (RedisBus when REDIS_URL, in-process otherwise). Renamed voice/fleet_events.py; publishes door decisions, handoffs, skill activations for Floor/observers. Redis stays optional (C4); nothing on the audio path waits on it. A2A (agent_core/a2a.py) remains the only agent-to-agent channel that leaves the process, and only off the audio path.
runtime_model:
A. INBOUND VOICE
1. Connect (bot.py run_bot). Today: load_active_bundle('production') at :427 before the caller is known, bot_id from bundle or DEFAULT_BOT_ID at :444-447, caller lookup at :504. New order: read Twilio params → twilio_ops.lookup_customer_for_caller → door.resolve(channel='voice', to_number, features) → target bot_id → load_active_bundle(bot_id, customer_id) (canary split per card via canary.pick_deployment_id) → door_decisions row + interactions.fleet_release_id stamp (persist.start_voice_call). Tier 0 hits (known borrower, DPD>0, collections line → Collections; open lead or product-interest flag → Insurance; callback_pending → the card that scheduled it) cost no hop. No rule → Door Card (intake-v1), never Collections by default.
2. Prefix. _system_instruction_from_bundle (bot.py:80-105) builds prompt + persona + guardrails + skill description block; identical per deployment, so it is a prompt-cache hit whenever prefix_warm has kept that card hot on this worker. resolve_mouth → ToolGrant → build_authored_flow(entry: isStart node or mission entryFor) exactly as bot.py:1134-1195 does today.
3. Door Card path (Tier 1). greet_disclose (disclose_recording) → discover_intent (capture_call_goal, deterministic intent.resolve_intent on the goal text — synchronous and cheap; understanding.analyze_turn's LLM refinement lands a turn late and only corrects the record) → verify_identity (intake's human gate on handoff_to_agent requires identity, defaults.py:171) → expression edge on call_goal_intent → 'handoff' action with target from door_rules. The model never picks the target. Carry built by the runtime; Bundle Swap; the handoff node's entryLine ('One moment, connecting you to our collections team') is spoken from TTS while the swap runs, so the caller hears no gap.
4. Specialist card. Skills activate by authored activation rules: node entry (post-action) or intent or variable → load_skill semantics (developer message swap, offer narrows/widens within the grant, prefix untouched). Skill-to-skill inside a card carries data through the FlowVariables bag — no hop, no cache cost. Locked engines run as today: reco/authority via tools, treatment/live_qa in code.
5. Boundary hop mid-call (e.g. Collections → Insurance after PTP). Eligibility: node lists handoff_to_agent or reco returns a shortlist → prefetch target bundle/grant/flow. Trigger: flow edge (expression on reco_shortlist non-empty and upsell_blocked empty and promotional consent present) or the model calling handoff_to_agent with target ∈ card.handoffs (allowlist as today, domain.py:1009). Runtime check at the edge: contact_policy promotional consent (REASON_NO_PROMO_CONSENT exists for outbound; the in-call equivalent is added) and mission.NEVER_OFFER. Swap under Carry: identity carried, target lands on its handoff entry node (skips verify), same TTS voice unless the edge says switch, announce_line spoken. interactions.handler_bot_id updated (db_inbox.py:1441) as today, plus handoff_events. Return hop (Insurance → Collections 'caller returns to dues') is the same mechanism; max_hops_per_call caps ping-pong.
6. Close. end_call → CrmSink complete → call_closer writes call_outcomes (connection/business axes) with hops → post_call_actions runs the last handler card's on_outcome verbs; cadence reads the mission card; voice/memory writes the cross-call memory card; Supervisor brief card renders the warm-transfer brief from the Carry when escalation was warm.

B. OUTBOUND
1. treatment engine → Action Contract (decision_id, objective, policy_version). 2. door.resolve_outbound(objective, pool) → the one production card declaring it (G-OB10). 3. mission.build (card entry_node, allowed_offers, authority_profile, max_duration) → outbound.dial: reserve → contact_policy.admit → suppress-on-refusal → place (the single owner sequence TARGET-ARCHITECTURE NEW #1 names) → call_attempts(bot_id, deployment_id, objective, decision_id, policy_version, fleet_release_id). 4. Answer → bot.py reads attempt_id/objective (:487-499) → load bundle by the attempt's deployment_id → mission briefing developer message → entryFor node (confirm_identity or an authored per-mission door). 5. Skills as A.4 (hardship_declared on a dpd_reminder is a skill activation inside Collections, not a hop; a hop to Insurance is only reachable when mission.allowed_offers is non-empty and the objective is not in NEVER_OFFER). 6. Close as A.6; cadence retries the same mission; exhaustion → treatment/followthrough decides.

C. WHATSAPP TURN
1. Webhook → bot_worker → handle_turn. Today bot_runtime.py:712 loads the bundle by env _bot_id(). New: conversations.handler_bot_id (sticky) → if null, door.resolve(channel='whatsapp', features, first-message intent from analyze_turn — text is off the audio path so the LLM classifier is fine here) → set handler, door_decisions row → load_active_bundle(bot_id, customer_id). Each turn stamps fleet_release_id on the message/job.
2. flow_text.py: current node from bot_state → node instruction as developer message, offer = grant ∩ node tools ∪ globals, go_to_* transition tools, expression/always edges evaluated after tool results; skill activation as on voice (bot_runtime.py:909-945 already resolves the active skill per turn).
3. Handoff on text: bot_tools._tool_handoff_to_agent (today sets ctx.bot_id for the rest of the turn only) → writes conversations.handler_bot_id + handoff_events with Carry → same job re-assembles messages with the target bundle and answers in the receiving card's voice (one extra LLM call, acceptable off-audio). Next turn loads the target directly.
4. Close on text: conversation close job → Closer path with channel='whatsapp' → same outcome vocabulary and post_call rules.
studio_model:
SCREENS. The 26 /agent-studio routes (main.py:2106-2426) and the fleet index (Habibi/src/routes/agent-studio.index.tsx) become three fleet-level screens plus the card editor plus the skills library.
1. Fleet map — the existing AgentGraph data (api/agent-studio.ts:308, /agent-studio/cards/{bot_id}/graph) extended with the Door as a node, door rules as labelled inbound edges, handoff edges labelled with carry schema and entry node, and skills drawn inside each card as 'specialist (skill)' chips so the owner sees twelve specialists without twelve compliance units. Reachability lozenges stay (entry/handoff/direct/unreachable) with 'entry' now meaning 'has a door rule'.
2. Door — a rules table (channel, number/pool, conditions form over the fixed feature vocabulary, first-utterance intent from the understanding allowed list, target card) with priority ordering, a default row per channel (seeded from today's BOT_ID), a 'Who answers this?' simulator (paste a customer id or features → resolved rule/card), and outbound objective ownership (which card dials which objective per pool; G-OB10 conflicts shown inline).
3. Releases — fleet_releases list, diff between two releases (which cards/skills/door rows changed), and the regulator lookup: paste an interaction, attempt or message id → release → per-turn card deployment, active skill version, flow node, decision_id, policy_version, door rule.
4. Card editor — the fifteen tabs in prompt-studio.lazy.tsx:1109-1132 stay. Changes: 'Agent graph' becomes 'Handoffs' (per edge: target, when, entry node picker from the target's graph, carry schema form, announce line, voice keep/switch, promotional-consent requirement flag); 'Skills' becomes a skill graph within the card (attached packs, activation rules per pack, exit carry, per-skill eval status, prefix budget meter G6/G21, 'Promote to card' when an author asks for a distinct persona or data_class); 'Flow' gains the handoff entry node type and shows skill entry nodes as lanes; 'Outbound' shows objective ownership; 'Ship' shows the new gates, eval-cache provenance ('regression pass · cached r-… unchanged since 2026-08-30'), the canary slice (only this card's door share) and a preview of the fleet release the publish will create.
5. Skills library — the existing create/patch/sign/clone/attach/export routes (main.py:2301-2426) get an activation editor (form fields only: intents from the understanding vocabulary, nodes from the host card, objectives from flow_graph.OBJECTIVES, variables from SESSION_VARIABLES ∪ extract variables), an eval fixture builder (tool-sequence and CRM-row expectations feeding eval/graders.py code graders), and signing gated by the skill.sign permission (compliance officer role).

ADDING A SPECIALIST (no code). Example: mandate re-registration specialist for Collections. Author: Skills → New → name/description (lint caps 120 tokens) → allowed-tools picker (catalog ∩ Collections include∪locked, so G9 cannot fail later) → activation: objective=mandate_reregistration OR nonpayment_reason=mandate_broken OR node=state_position with intent=mandate_broken → body steps and never-list → three fixtures minimum (verify before any write; no product named — NEVER_OFFER; required tool order) → run skill suite in sandbox → compliance officer signs → attach to the Collections draft → Ship. Compiler: G9 signed and in scope, G19 activation valid and non-conflicting, G6/G21 idle-tool and prefix budgets, G7 regression via cached card report plus the new skill suite, G8 redteam cached (boundary unchanged), G12 canary at the chosen slice → publish creates a new fleet release. If instead the author needs a different persona name, a marketing data_class or a different authority profile, G16 refuses the skill route with 'boundary differs' and the studio offers Clone from template (agent_core/cards/templates.py, clone.py: Collections/Lapse/Hardship/Clerk) — the full card pipeline, deliberately more expensive because it is a real compliance boundary.

WHAT THE COMPILER CHECKS, in order: G0 schema, G1 flow valid, G2 flow persisted, G3 policy bindings all 'required', G4 tools in catalog, G5 handoff targets exist, G16 boundary distinct, G17 door coverage, G18 carry compatibility and hop cycle cap, G19 skill activation, G6 latency budgets, G21 prefix budget, G9 signed skills, G10 connectors, G7/G8/G11 evals with G20 cache provenance, G-OB1–10 outbound, G12 canary, G13 A2A mTLS, G14 publish permission, G15 voice locale. First red stops mutation; the report lists every static failure.
handoff_mechanics:
WHAT CHANGES ON A HOP (voice/handoff.py swap), dimension by dimension:
- Prompt: the system role message is replaced with the target deployment's _system_instruction_from_bundle output (prompt + persona + guardrails + its skill description block). The context is rebuilt as: target system prefix → Carry as one fenced developer message (identity, goal, intent, language, mission constraints, deterministic extractive summary from compaction.bound_history, SQL open commitments) → the last N=8 raw turns kept verbatim (card.memory.compaction.raw_last_n). No LLM summariser on the hop path; the analysis-profile summary lands later in context_summaries for the record. Pipecat mechanics: the target graph's NodeConfigs carry the new role message, so flow_manager.set_node_from_config to the handoff entry node is the swap; the same call flows_dynamic already uses for 'always' edges.
- Tools: new ToolGrant.for_bundle(target, 'voice'); voice/tools.build_tools rebuilds the registry filtered by that grant ∪ VOICE_ALWAYS (tools.py:2916-2919); node functions come from the target graph; global functions replaced. Nothing carries over — the grant is derived from the target card (ADR-0001), and the Carry has no tool field.
- Flow: build_authored_flow(target flow, entry_node = edge.entry_node or the node with entryFor ['handoff']); the FlowVariables bag is seeded from carry.flow_variables so expression edges on the target see identity_verified='true', call_goal, intent immediately.
- Voice: default keep the current TTS voice (a caller hearing a new voice mid-sentence is a product decision, not a technical default); an edge with voice=switch sends TTSUpdateSettingsFrame with the target deployment's ttsVoiceId; the announce_line is spoken by the handing-off card as the node entryLine so the swap runs under speech.
- Context/session: session.deployment_id, session.extra['bot_id'], interactions.handler_bot_id and transferred_from_bot_id (sql/04_interactions.sql:8-9, db_inbox.py:1441), handoff_events row, RTVI lifecycle(phase='handoff') for the Floor, fleet event publish. identity_verified on the session is set from carry.identity only when the Carry was built by the runtime in the same interaction.

WHAT IT COSTS (per hop, not per turn):
- Bundle load ~10–30 ms (two SQL reads, cached after prefetch), grant build <1 ms, flow compile ~10–30 ms, registry rebuild <5 ms — all hidden under the announce line when prefetched.
- LLM first token on the new prefix: a prompt-cache MISS on the target prefix unless warm. On a 2–3k-token prefix the hit/miss delta on the voice deployment is roughly 100–300 ms TTFT (measure; do not assume). With prefix_warm keeping every active production card hot on the worker, the common case is a hit; the honest worst case is one cold miss per hop.
- After the hop every subsequent turn is a normal cached turn on the target's prefix — the same 30-turn cache survival the skills runtime was built for.
- Hop count is bounded by card.memory.max_hops_per_call (default 2; G18 warns on graphs that allow more), so a call pays at most two misses and typically zero or one.

WHAT IS AMORTISED AND HOW: per-card warm prefixes (publish-time prime + periodic keep-warm ≤ cache idle TTL, extending the existing boot warm at bot.py:2455-2510); prefetch at edge eligibility (node lists handoff_to_agent, reco shortlist non-empty); deterministic Carry (no summariser call on the hop); bridging announce line spoken during the swap; Tier-0 Door so most inbound calls land on the right card with zero hops; skills for everything inside a boundary at zero prefix cost. On-prem (C4): vLLM automatic prefix caching is process-local, so warming and hops must stay on the same engine worker — the swap is in-process, so they do.

WHERE IT CANNOT GO, said plainly: a different persona is a different prefix; there is no way to have both a distinct compliance boundary and a shared cache line. So the design keeps boundaries few, hops rare, and each hop bounded and measured (handoff_events.prefix_cache_hit, hop_ms feed the canary's slo_miss trigger). The Insurance sidecar LLMWorker (voice/workers/insurance.py) is not the answer: a second process needs Redis (C4 says optional), doubles the warm problem, and still changes the prefix the caller's turn is generated against.

TEXT (WhatsApp): no cache constraint; the hop is handler switch + handoff_events + one extra assembly with the target bundle in the same job.
audit_model:
One number per contact: fleet_release_id. It is written in the same transaction as the publish that produced it (the pattern agent_core/change_log.py already uses: hashes not copies, prev_hash chain, verify_chain), and stamped on interactions (persist.start_voice_call), call_attempts (outbound.reserve — beside bot_id, deployment_id, objective, decision_id, policy_version at sql/21_outbound.sql:27-46), conversations/messages per WhatsApp turn (a conversation spanning a publish is answered per turn, so a message resolves to the release live when it was generated), door_decisions and handoff_events.
The manifest resolves everything else without guessing: door_version → the rule that chose the card; cards{bot_id} → deployment_id → prompt_versions row (immutable once published: prompt, persona, voice, guardrails, flow, agent_card, tuning) → skill_version_ids (signed content_hash bodies) → grader_version → policy_version.
Per-turn attribution inside a multi-agent call comes from handoff_events turn ranges (from/to deployment_id, turn_index) plus the existing turn trace (bot_tool_calls, get_turn_trace) extended with active_skill_version_id so 'which skill body was in context when this sentence was spoken' is a row, not an inference. The Closer writes call_outcomes.hops so an outcome is attributed to the card that produced it while the mission's card owns cadence.
The three regulator questions: 'why this sentence' → interaction → release → turn → card deployment + skill version + flow node + live_qa verdict; 'why this offer' → reco decision log keyed by decision_id (unchanged) + carry.reco_shortlist_ids proving the target card received a shortlist, not a product name; 'why this call at this time' → call_attempts.decision_id + policy_version + contact_policy admit/suppress row + cadence state + the objective-owner card in the release.
What is deliberately NOT fragmented: the door does not create a second routing table (rules are versioned rows in the release); the Carry is stored verbatim; the mesh's in-memory history (mesh.py MeshState.history, lost at release_session) is replaced by durable rows. Honest residue: a canary split means two deployments of one card are live inside one release — the release records both and the interaction records which one it got (deployment_id), as today.
policy_model:
Engines stay code with a log, unchanged: reco (recommend_next_offer), treatment (recommend_treatment), authority (evaluate_authority), live_qa (evaluate_live_qa) locked on every card (schema.LOCKED_POLICY_ENGINES, G3 all 'required'); contact_policy.admit is the only gate before any dial or send.
What the new pieces may and may not decide:
- The Door picks a card, never an action, product, time or channel. Its features are read-only CRM facts; its output is a bot_id. Outbound: the door runs after treatment has produced the Action Contract and before contact_policy.admit, inside outbound.dial's fixed sequence, so it cannot bypass either.
- A Carry cannot widen anything. It has no tool field; the grant is derived from the target card. identity.verified is honoured only when the Carry was built by voice/handoff.py or bot_tools.py in the same interaction from session.identity_verified — model arguments to handoff_to_agent are target and reason only, and a carry-shaped string in a payload is dropped. Mission constraints travel with the Carry and are re-imposed on the target (allowed_offers, NEVER_OFFER, max_duration_sec, upsell_blocked), and reco is locked on the target so an Insurance card that receives a hardship caller still gets an empty shortlist.
- Skill activation is offer-only. It can put a body in context and narrow or restore the offer within the grant; it cannot add a tool, unlock an engine, or skip a human gate. Activation rules cannot reference locked engines.
- Human gates (card.human_gates require identity|floor|both) are enforced at execution in ToolGrant.may_execute / domain dispatch as today. A carried identity satisfies require='identity' only with method ∈ VERIFY_METHODS from this interaction; require='floor' is never satisfiable by a Carry — the floor is asked.
- Identity-before-writes stays mechanical: every card that is a handoff target has an entry node that either verifies or is reached only with carry.identity.verified (G18), and node_contracts.NODE_REQUIRED keeps every node leaveable under a narrow grant.
- Promotional boundary: an edge into a card with data_class 'marketing' requires promotional consent at the edge (the in-call sibling of contact_policy.REASON_NO_PROMO_CONSENT) and G18 requires the flag; hardship latch and mission.NEVER_OFFER veto the edge at runtime regardless of what the model asks.
- live_qa runs per turn on whichever card is speaking; its escalate/hold nudges (_live_escalate in bot.py) are card-agnostic.
- G16 is itself a policy control: it stops authority or data_class differences from being smuggled in as a skill, because a skill cannot carry an authority envelope.
eval_model:
Three tiers, each keyed by content hash so cost tracks change, not fleet size.
1. Skill suite (kind=regression, id skill.<slug>, already named in frontmatter eval_suite) — fixtures are tool-call sequences and CRM-row expectations run by the existing code graders (eval/graders.py, harness.py; no LLM). Runs when the skill version's content_hash changes. Owned by the skill author; minimum three fixtures to sign.
2. Card suite — regression = card boundary tasks (identity before write, no prose handoff, DND, injection via CRM card) ∪ the attached skills' suites by reference; redteam = boundary attacks only (eval/critique.py's seven lines: verify_before_ptp, dnd, no_prose_handoff, crm_card_injection, product_in_reco, hardship_hold, skill_jailbreak). eval_reports gains content_key = hash(card_hash, flow_hash, sorted skill_version_ids, grader_version); G20 lets G7/G8 pass on a stored passing report with the same key and reports it as 'pass · cached' with the report id — never 'skipped'. eval/run.py already notes suites are one-to-many across cards (nine cards name eval-regression-collections), which is exactly the sharing this formalises.
3. Fleet suite — door fixtures ((channel, features, first utterance) → expected card) and carry fixtures (identity never widened; mission constraints preserved; hop cap honoured). Runs when door_rules or any handoff edge changes.
Canary (canary.py, six triggers incl. slo_miss fed by handoff_events.hop_ms) applies to the changed card's deployment only, at that card's door share; attaching a skill to Collections is one Collections canary, not a fleet canary. The twin (agent_core/twin.py) stays for outbound ladders (G-OB9/G11) and is unaffected by skill count.
Cost of adding a specialist as a skill: its own ~10 fixtures + one host-card compile with cached regression/redteam + one canary — O(1). Cost of adding a boundary card: full card suite + redteam + canary — deliberately O(card), because G16 only lets a real boundary through. The sub-linearity claim is honest only if grader_version is part of the cache key (a grader fix invalidates every cached report, as it should) and if fixtures are graded on tool calls and CRM rows rather than transcripts (they are today).

risks: Prompt-cache warming is provider behaviour, not a contract: Azure's cache is evicted after 5–10 min idle and needs a ≥1024-token prefix; vLLM prefix caching is per engine process. If warming does not hold, a hop costs a cold miss (~+100–300 ms TTFT on a 2–3k prefix) once per hop. handoff_events.prefix_cache_hit and hop_ms must be measured from Phase 3 day one and fed to the canary.

A persona change mid-call is a disclosure question the technical design cannot settle: recording was disclosed by 'Priya'; whether 'my colleague from insurance' needs fresh promotional consent under DPDP is the compliance officer's call. The design makes it a required flag on the edge (G18) and defaults to keep-voice, but the decision has to be made before Insurance is reachable in production.

Deterministic door misroutes: a Tier-0 rule that sends a borrower with a product question to Collections turns a zero-hop call into a one-hop call. Mitigation is the Door Card fallback and the fleet suite's door fixtures, not confidence.

flow_text.py is the largest genuinely new construction, on a path (bot_worker) whose logs are currently discarded (root logger has no handler). Ship the logging fix first or Phase 4 regressions are silent.

Eval caching by content hash goes stale silently if grader_version is left out of the key or fixtures grade transcripts instead of tool calls/CRM rows. The design requires both; a future contributor can undo either in one line.

Releases and long-lived WhatsApp threads: a conversation that spans a publish is stamped per turn, so 'which release answered this conversation' has several answers. That is the truthful shape, but the Releases screen must present it as such or an auditor will read the last stamp as the only one.

Deleting the Insurance sidecar removes the only multi-process specialist demo the codebase has. The honest position is that voice latency (C1) and Redis-optional (C4) both point to in-process swaps; anyone selling 'agents as separate services' loses a slide.

Hop ping-pong (Collections ↔ Insurance) is bounded by max_hops_per_call, but the bound ends the hop, not the call — the caller stays with whichever card they are on. The UX of a refused hop needs an authored line on the edge.

G16 will be argued with: an insurance ops lead who wants a 'lapse specialist' with its own name will hear 'that is a skill'. Templates (Lapse Specialist in templates.py) already exist to say yes when the boundary is real; the studio must make the distinction legible or authors will route around it.

Migration hygiene per repo memory: additive tables only, never run migrations while the corpus simulator runs, and every carved module reaches the engine through db, not a direct import, or the test suite's savepoint proxy stops wrapping writes.

The fleet stays small by design (4–8 cards). If the product owner's picture of 'agentic' is a dozen visibly separate agents, the Fleet map's skill chips are the answer; if it is a dozen separate voices and authorities, this design refuses on purpose and says why (C1, C6).
score_self: C1 Voice latency: 4 — skill specialisation stays at zero prefix cost; a boundary hop is one bounded, warmed, prefetched, speech-covered cache miss at most twice per call; not 5 because a distinct persona is a distinct prefix and no design changes that.

C2 One version number: 4 — fleet_release_id pins door, every card deployment, flow, skill versions and grader/policy versions in one hash-chained row, and handoff_events gives per-turn attribution; not 5 because a canary split still means two live deployments of one card inside a release and WhatsApp threads are stamped per turn.

C3 Policy engines decide: 5 — engines unchanged and locked on every card; the door picks cards not actions; the Carry cannot widen and identity comes only from the runtime; human gates enforced at execution; promotional edges gated at the edge.
C4 On-prem deployability: 5 — Postgres tables, in-process swap, Redis optional (fleet events only), prefix warming works on vLLM's per-process cache, no managed agent cloud anywhere.

C5 Operator authorability: 4 — every new concept is a form over a fixed vocabulary (door features, intents, nodes, tool picker, fixture builder) with gates that refuse rather than warn; not 5 because activation rules and carry schemas are new ideas for an ops lead and the studio has to teach them.

C6 Sub-linear eval cost: 4 — skill suites plus hash-cached card reports plus boundary-only redteam make a new specialist O(1); a new boundary card is O(card) by design, and correctness depends on grader_version in the cache key.

C7 Migration realism: 4 — six flagged, additive, individually reversible phases naming the files and line sites; the flows.py deletion depends on a parity report that could stall, and Phase 4 sits on a path with no logging today.

C8 Inbound and outbound: 4 — door for inbound, objective ownership for outbound, typed Carry, Closer hops, and a text flow projection so WhatsApp finally runs the flow; the WhatsApp half is the least proven and the Door Card path adds a hop to unknown-caller calls.
